'''Hilary Ann Priestley''' is a British mathematician.  She is a professor at the [[University of Oxford]] and a Fellow of [[St Anne's College, Oxford]], where she has been Tutor in Mathematics since 1972.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gardam|first=Tim|title=Titles of Distinction awarded to eight Fellows|url=http://www.st-annes.ox.ac.uk/about/news/item/article/titles-of-distinction-awarded-to-ei|date=11 July 2006|access-date=11 June 2014|archive-date=18 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140618101946/http://www.st-annes.ox.ac.uk/about/news/item/article/titles-of-distinction-awarded-to-ei|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hilary Priestley introduced ordered [[Separable space|separable topological spaces]]; such topological spaces are now usually called [[Priestley space]]s in her honour.<ref>{{cite journal| journal=[[Semigroup Forum]] | date=December 1980 | volume=20 | number=1 | pages=293–297 | title=A partially ordered space which is not a Priestley space<!-- This reference uses all-caps for its title and consistently capitalizes "Priestley space" in its text; the lowercase "priestley" on the publisher landing page appears to be a publisher error. --> | first=Albert | last=Stralka | publisher=[[Springer (publisher)|Springer]] | doi=10.1007/BF02572690 | s2cid=123310469 }}</ref> The term "[[Priestley duality]]" is also used for her application of these spaces in the [[Distributive lattice#representation theory|representation theory of distributive lattices]].<ref>{{cite journal| journal=[[Order (journal)|Order]] | date=September 1991 | volume=8 | number=3 | pages=299–315 | title=Remarks on Priestley duality for distributive lattices | first1=R. | last1=Cignoli | first2=S. | last2=Lafalce | first3=A. | last3=Petrovich | publisher=[[Springer (publisher)|Springer]] | doi=10.1007/BF00383451 | s2cid=122146613 }}</ref>
